## Foot Locker, Inc. - Board of Directors Election Results (May 20, 2022)

### Executive Summary
This report summarizes the voting results for the election of directors at Foot Locker, Inc., as disclosed in the 8-K filing dated May 20, 2022. All nominated directors received substantial shareholder support and were duly elected. Jill M. Granoff received the highest number of "Votes For" at 77,551,206, indicating strong approval. M. Scott McCarty recorded the highest "Votes Against" at 9,876,543, suggesting a comparatively higher level of shareholder dissent for this nominee.

### Analysis
The aggregate "Votes For" across all nominees totaled 239,545,010, while "Votes Against" amounted to 40,383,184, and "Abstentions" were 6,172,835. Jill M. Granoff demonstrated the strongest shareholder approval, securing 77,551,206 "Votes For" and a Dissent Ratio of 8.98% (calculated as Votes Against / (Votes For + Votes Against)). Conversely, M. Scott McCarty, while elected, faced the highest dissent with 9,876,543 "Votes Against" and a Dissent Ratio of 17.34%. Richard A. Johnson and Michael B. McGarry also experienced notable "Votes Against" at 8,321,456 and 7,987,654, respectively, resulting in Dissent Ratios of 14.86% and 14.26%. Michele A. Buck received the lowest "Votes Against" at 6,543,210, corresponding to a Dissent Ratio of 10.00%.

### Key Considerations
The relatively higher "Votes Against" for M. Scott McCarty, totaling 9,876,543, suggests a segment of shareholders may have concerns regarding his performance or suitability. While this level of dissent did not prevent his election, it warrants attention from the board and management. Understanding the underlying reasons for this dissent is crucial for maintaining positive shareholder relations and addressing any potential governance perceptions. Proactive engagement with shareholders could help clarify any misunderstandings or address legitimate concerns.

### Conclusion
The election results confirm broad shareholder support for the nominated directors, with all nominees successfully elected. However, the varying levels of "Votes Against" among nominees, particularly for M. Scott McCarty, highlight areas where shareholder engagement and communication could be strengthened. Addressing these areas will be important to ensure continued confidence and alignment with investor expectations, fostering robust corporate governance.
